rcc.title: School Appraisal: Reviewer Calibration & Certification Framework 26-27

essentials.title: Review open and overdue actions in the action tracker
essentials.description: Start the week with what is still open: actions from visits, meetings and the Academic Board. Keep the evidence and links in the approved workspace, not in personal storage.

source.quote: Review open actions and overdue items in the Deliverables & Action Tracker.

essentials.title: Answer school and department questions and record decisions
essentials.description: Reply to the academic questions from your schools and departments. When an answer is a material decision, write it down in the approved record, not only in WhatsApp.

source.quote: Respond to school / department academic questions and record material decisions.

essentials.title: Check curriculum pacing and your assessment-production tasks
essentials.description: Look at where your subject's classes are against the Annual Plan, and at the questions and papers you owe. A gap you see early can still be closed.

source.quote: Review current curriculum pacing and assessment-production tasks.

essentials.title: Escalate material risks early, with evidence
essentials.description: Escalate a serious Cambridge compliance risk, a curriculum gap, repeated assessment problems, a safeguarding concern or repeated non-implementation. Say what the evidence is, the impact, what you have tried, your recommended next step and how urgent it is.
essentials.timing_text: Whenever an issue appears — do not wait for the next meeting

source.quote: Escalate when an issue is material, repeated, high-risk, or cannot be resolved at the Subject Specialist level.

essentials.title: Submit each visit report within 5 working days
essentials.description: Everything in the report must already have been said to the school in the feedback meeting: no surprises. Include strengths, no more than three priorities and agreed next steps with an owner and a date; the school receives a copy.

source.quote: Your visit report must be submitted to the Eduversal Academic Department within 5 working days of the visit.

tasks.title: Review your assigned schools and departments
tasks.description: Look at each school's pacing, assessment readiness, teaching-quality patterns, resource needs and unresolved actions in your subject. Departments are measured against the published standard, never ranked against each other.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month

source.quote: Review assigned schools / departments for curriculum pacing, assessment readiness, teaching-quality patterns, resource needs, and unresolved actions.

tasks.title: Read the latest Cambridge updates for your subject
tasks.description: Check the School Support Hub, new specimen or past papers and any examiner report. Read each examiner report within two weeks of release and add the common errors to your running notes for visits and question writing.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month, and whenever Cambridge releases something new

source.quote: Review Cambridge subject updates, examiner reports, or relevant support materials when released.

tasks.title: Prepare the next national subject department meeting
tasks.description: Build the agenda from what the evidence shows — pacing, Common Assessment results, visit patterns — not from general announcements. Record the decisions and actions in the department meeting record afterwards.
tasks.timing_text: In the week before each Saturday National Subject Department meeting (22 Aug, 19 Sep, 21 Nov 2026; 23 Jan, 27 Feb, 10 Apr 2027)

source.quote: Prepare the next department / subject network meeting agenda from evidence, not from general announcements.

tasks.title: Keep Teacher-Paced Test questions ahead of the vet-and-set deadline
tasks.description: Check which chapters finish in the coming weeks and that their questions are drafted, peer-reviewed and submitted on time. A test submitted late is not approved in time and is not published.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: check once a month; each submission is due two weeks before the chapter completion week

source.quote: The vet-and-set submission deadline closes two weeks before the chapter completion week indicated in the Annual Plan.

tasks.title: Review Common Assessment results after each test window
tasks.description: Look for chapters that are weak across the network and schools or classes far from the network picture, then share what you see with the Academic Coordinator and Principal and propose support. The data is read at school and network level, never to rate a teacher.
tasks.timing_text: After each test window closes (suggested: check once a month)

source.quote: Review results after each test window; identify patterns across schools

tasks.title: Assign this year's Common Assessment authors, chapter by chapter
tasks.description: Every chapter in the annual sequence for your subject should have a named author and a draft date before teaching reaches it. Teachers may draft questions, but you remain the quality owner.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year, at the first subject meeting

source.quote: At the first DTP meeting of the academic year, assign chapter-by-chapter question-writing responsibilities across the full annual sequence for your subject.

tasks.title: Set your 2–3 professional growth goals in your IPDL
tasks.description: Make the goals outcome-based, linked to a real gap and measurable within the year. Record each PD activity with an impact statement, not only a title and a date.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: At the start of each academic year, set 2–3 specific professional improvement goals.

tasks.title: Hold your termly IPDL review with the Academic Director
tasks.description: Bring your IPDL evidence, an honest self-assessment and specific questions about your own reports, visits or sessions. Check whether your domain alignment map shows any neglected area.
tasks.timing_text: Once a term (shown near the end of each semester)

source.quote: Use your termly review as a genuine development conversation, not a compliance meeting.

tasks.title: Complete your reviewer calibration before the first visits
tasks.description: Work through the shared evidence pack on your own first, then discuss it. Walkthrough reviewers also do a shared classroom scenario, and Domain Leads complete at least two domain scenarios before confirming domain judgements independently.
tasks.timing_text: Before the first School Appraisal cycle of the year (Phase 1 starts 5 August 2026)

source.quote: All current School Appraisal reviewers complete one baseline evidence-pack calibration.

tasks.title: Take part in the mid-year calibration check
tasks.description: Use it to look at where reviewers' judgements differed in the Phase 1 and Phase 3 visits. It is a quality-assurance step, not an appraisal of you.
tasks.timing_text: Mid-year, after the Semester I visits

source.quote: A short mid-year calibration check is used to address any recurring variance from Phase 1 and Phase 3 visits.

tasks.title: Run the Phase 0 Kickoff for the schools you supervise
tasks.description: With the CAO, introduce the cycle, the school's two Supervisors, the self-appraisal across all five domains and the evidence deadlines. Schools are grouped in online batches of three to four.
tasks.timing_text: About three weeks before each school's Phase 1 visit (15 July – 27 August 2026)

source.quote: Conduct Phase 0 Kickoff sessions — all 15 schools

tasks.title: Observe lessons formatively on this week's Teaching Quality Visits
tasks.description: Before each visit read the last report and review the evidence for your domain; on the day, observe 35–45 minutes per lesson and hold the Glow / Grow / Go conversation the same or the next day. Your observation never creates or changes a teacher's F2 score.
tasks.timing_text: Each week of the Phase 1 window (5 August – 18 September 2026) in which you are on a visit team

source.quote: It gives the teacher direct Glow/Grow/Go feedback and, at school level, is used to validate the school's aggregated F2 picture

tasks.title: Lead the Phase 2 Progress Check-in for your Visit I schools
tasks.description: Hold a 1–2 hour online meeting midway between the school's Phase 1 and Phase 3 visits. Review previous actions and progress across D1–D5, record it in the Progress Check-in Record and do not re-score any domain.
tasks.timing_text: On each school's Phase 2 date (4 September – 16 October 2026); all check-ins completed by 18 October

source.quote: The Visit I Supervisor schedules the Zoom meeting with the School Principal and Academic Coordinator.

tasks.title: Validate the evidence and set Final Ratings for your domain
tasks.description: Lead your Domain Meeting, set the verification for each evidence item and rate each aspect from the evidence quality, not from the Suggested Rating alone. Explain any gap of 1.0 or more in the Domain Lead Comment column.
tasks.timing_text: Each week of the Phase 3 window (7 October – 20 November 2026) in which you are on a visit team

source.quote: Sets the Eduversal Final Rating (1–4) for each aspect in the Scoring sheet, using the Suggested Rating as a starting point, not a fixed answer.

tasks.title: Write the Annual School Quality Report for your Visit I schools
tasks.description: Add the commendations, up to three recommendations, the two School Development Priorities and the action plan to the five domain ratings. Each domain keeps its own Development Rating — never an overall school score.
tasks.timing_text: Within 3 weeks of each school's Phase 3 visit; every report is due by 11 December 2026

source.quote: Visit I Supervisor only: writes the Annual School Quality Report within 3 weeks of the Phase 3 visit.

tasks.title: Enter the Scorecard Layer figures for your domain
tasks.description: Enter only the raw values that exist and leave an unmeasurable cell empty, never 0. The figures are reporting-only this year and carry no weight in the Development Rating.
tasks.timing_text: After each Validation Visit, before the school's report is written

source.quote: The Domain Lead fills it in, and the numbers appear in School Appraisal: Annual School Quality Report 26-27 as supporting information.

tasks.title: Check progress on your schools' two Development Priorities
tasks.description: Look at the implementation evidence with the Principal and Academic Coordinator and log anything important as a Coordinator Note. If a school's outcome status moves to Needs Support or Critical Attention, escalate to the CAO.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: mid-Semester II (Supervisors stay in regular contact all year)

source.quote: Reviewing the two School Development Priorities and their implementation evidence

tasks.title: Lead the Phase 4 Impact Review for your Visit I schools
tasks.description: Review what was implemented for the two priorities, what changed and what evidence shows it, then agree an impact status and what carries forward. It does not reopen the Phase 3 ratings.
tasks.timing_text: May–June 2027, online (shown in the last teaching week)

source.quote: It is developmental only and creates no new Domain Rating. Led by the Visit I Supervisor with an Eduversal representative.

tasks.title: Get your Synchronized Test questions written, reviewed and approved
tasks.description: Each question is reviewed by at least one other Subject Specialist, the Academic Board confirms the final set and the CAO signs off before it is published. Where the live EASE Schedule replaces the test with a Cambridge exam, follow the schedule.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: about six weeks before EASE Week 2 (7–11 December 2026) and EASE Week 4 (10–14 May 2027)

source.quote: Subject Specialists write and vet the questions for their subject.

tasks.title: Support the EASE Growth week
tasks.description: Help with the scheduled EASE Growth and Teacher-Paced activities and answer school questions quickly. Protect exam-heavy grades from extra initiatives that week.
tasks.timing_text: Before EASE Week 1 (28 Sep – 2 Oct 2026) and EASE Week 3 (29 Mar – 2 Apr 2027)

source.quote: Support the scheduled EASE Growth / EASE Assessment activities according to the current EASE calendar.

tasks.title: Write the EASE Growth analysis for your domain
tasks.description: Applies if your subject is one of the three Growth domains. Version 1 is a baseline: never call a result growth, do not compare with a previous cycle unless the Academic Board has approved it, and never rank schools.
tasks.timing_text: Within 3 weeks of each Growth window closing: Growth I (by 23 Oct 2026), Primary Growth (early February 2027), Growth II (by 23 Apr 2027)

source.quote: It is produced within three weeks of each EASE Growth window closing and submitted to the Eduversal Academic Director.

tasks.title: Write and vet your subject's EASE Academic questions
tasks.description: Applies to the EASE Academic subjects. Check each question against the Exam Blueprint and the published preparation resources so the CAO can sign off in time.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: well before each sitting (5 December 2026 and 15 May 2027)

source.quote: Questions are written and vetted by Subject Specialists on the Academic Board, with final sign-off by the CAO.

tasks.title: Do one peer observation with a Specialist colleague
tasks.description: Observe independently, then debrief: what did each of you notice, and what would you have said differently in the feedback meeting? You can also swap a visit report or invite a colleague to a PD session.
tasks.timing_text: Once per term

source.quote: Once per term, arrange to accompany a colleague on a school visit — or invite a colleague to accompany you.

tasks.title: Review Department Performance with each Subject Leader
tasks.description: Go through the eight areas with the school's Subject Leader or HoD and agree a clear improvement action where the result is low. It is a support signal, not a teacher or School Appraisal score.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: mid-semester (it runs across the semester)

source.quote: The Subject Specialist works with the school’s Subject Leader/Head of Department and uses Department Performance as a semester-long operational and support framework.

tasks.title: Summarise your subject's Semester I patterns
tasks.description: Say what improved, what did not and what needs intervention next semester. Update your PD priorities from visit and assessment evidence and remove superseded working files.
tasks.timing_text: December, after the EASE cycle (shown in the last teaching week of Semester I)

source.quote: Summarise key subject-level patterns: what improved, what did not, and what needs intervention next semester.

tasks.title: Reset your Semester II priorities from the evidence
tasks.description: Reconfirm your high-priority schools and departments and the actions still open from Semester I. Check updated school calendars and external-exam pressure points, and confirm Semester II assessment-production timelines.
tasks.timing_text: January, start of Semester II

source.quote: Reconfirm high-priority schools / departments and unresolved Semester 1 actions.

tasks.title: Check syllabus coverage against external-exam timelines
tasks.description: Make sure the planned curriculum is being completed at the right depth in the time that is really left. Look at revision quality too: past papers, command words and practical readiness.
tasks.timing_text: March

source.quote: Verify syllabus coverage and pacing against external-exam timelines.

tasks.title: Complete your annual programme review
tasks.description: Record the evidence, impact, unresolved risks and recommendations, and note which question-bank, curriculum, resource or PD updates 27-28 will need. Make sure no high-risk issue is lost in the handover.
tasks.timing_text: May–June (shown in the last teaching week)

source.quote: Complete annual programme review: evidence, impact, unresolved risks, recommendations.

tasks.title: Refresh your subject's recommended network resources
tasks.description: Check that the resources you recommend still match the curriculum, and remove dead links and low-value tools. Subject resource maps should be reviewed at least once per semester.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a semester

source.quote: Subject Specialist / Academic Board: identifies strong network-level resources, checks curriculum alignment and periodically refreshes recommendations.

notes_for_reviewer: What was wrong in v1 (subject-specialist.json): (1) a 40-week year with fixed week numbers; the real year has 36 teaching weeks. (2) It made the Specialist a cross-school teacher appraiser ('primary appraiser', 'sync scores with the Subject Leader', F1 + F2 records); the live documents say Specialist observations are formative only and never create or change an F2 score. (3) It placed 'Sem-2 school appraisal visits Feb–Apr'; both on-site visits are in Semester I (Phase 1 5 Aug–18 Sep, Phase 3 7 Oct–20 Nov), Phase 2 is online and Phase 4 is May–June. (4) Invented duties with no live basis: Cambridge Oct/Nov entry sign-off (a Cambridge Coordinator / Exams Officer job), a monthly brief 'filed in subject_specialist_reports', weekly IPDL updates (live: termly review), 'compliance' priority and regulatory anchors. (5) 'Lead Sem-1 Common Assessment cycle in November'; the live model is Teacher-Paced Tests through the semester plus the Synchronized Test in EASE Week 2 (7–11 Dec), with CAO sign-off. (6) The induction overlay (Level 4 Lead mentor, 10-walkthrough cycle, Q4 evaluation by an 'HQ Director', NN1–NN3 citations) does not match Induction Module: Specialists 26-27 (five phases, Mentor Specialist, Academic Director, SS-NN codes).

Titles: 'Academic Board: Quality Oversight 26-27' and 'Appraisal Suite: Annual Network Quality Report Framework 26-27' are the Drive names from ab-export/_index.json; the first line inside each export is shorter ('Quality Oversight 26-27', 'Annual Network Quality Report Framework 26-27'). 'Teacher Development: Capacity-Building Guide 26-27' (SS2-034) is derived from the export file name; other live documents call it 'Teacher Capacity-Building Guide 26-27' — please confirm the Drive title.

National Subject Department meeting dates in SS2-008 (22 Aug, 19 Sep, 21 Nov 2026; 23 Jan, 27 Feb, 10 Apr 2027, all Saturdays) come from the Academic Board Master Timeline (a Sheet). The quote comes from the Annual Operating Calendar's monthly rhythm, which asks for an evidence-based agenda but gives no dates. 22 Aug and 19 Sep are already past.

Synchronized Test lead time (SS2-024): the Specialist Guide production table says 'EASE Paper … Yes — Academic Director sign-off … 6 weeks before EASE window', while EASE Assessment: Standards and the Guide's own Common Assessment row give final sign-off to the CAO after Academic Board vet-and-set. I used six weeks only as a suggestion in timing_text and named the CAO. Please decide which sign-off line is current and whether 'EASE Paper' in that table means the Synchronized Test.

Specialist Guide §5 'EASE Team Formation — Start-of-Year Requirement' reads as if addressed to schools ('teams … with designated leads for each EASE Growth cycle', 'distribution of question-drafting responsibilities across all teachers') and says past EASE papers should not be treated as confidential. That conflicts with EASE Growth secure-item rules (Service Gateway: 'Do not copy secure candidate items into school-facing materials'). Not used; the chapter-by-chapter Common Assessment author assignment (SS2-011) is used instead. The same section still says 'DTP meeting' (the quote in SS2-011 keeps it verbatim).

EASE Growth Analysis Report (SS2-026): the Specialist Guide template asks for 'Comparison to previous EASE Growth cycle' and 'Performance relative to the network mean'; the Working Tool: EASE Growth Analysis Report 26-27 says previous-cycle comparison is normally Not Applicable in Version 1. The description follows the Working Tool. The Primary Growth date differs between the brief (18–22 Jan 2027) and the calendar (17–21 Jan 2027); either way the 3-week deadline falls in early February, so the task shows in the 1 Feb week (8–12 Feb is the Ramadhan skip week).

'Termly' (SS2-013 IPDL review, SS2-028 peer observation): the documents do not define a term; I placed both once per semester. The visit report is 'submitted to the Eduversal Academic Department' in Specialist Guide §3 but to the 'Eduversal Academic Director' in the §7 deadline table — SS2-005 uses the §3 sentence.

School Appraisal role tasks apply only where the Specialist holds the role: Phase 0 Kickoff and Visit Supervisor duties (SS2-016), Phase 2 and Phase 4 for Visit I Supervisors (SS2-018, SS2-023), the Annual School Quality Report for Visit I Supervisors (SS2-020), Domain Lead Final Ratings and Scorecard entry (SS2-019, SS2-021; the Scorecard may also be completed by the CAO centrally). The weekly checklist cannot tell who is Visit I/II Supervisor for which school; consider a role filter or leave these as they are.

The ASQR reminder (SS2-020) shows on 2 Nov and 30 Nov because Phase 3 visits run from 7 Oct to 20 Nov and each report is due within 3 weeks of its own visit (all by 11 Dec). The Scorecard task (SS2-021) is placed once after the Phase 3 window; it really follows each Validation Visit.

Left out on purpose: 'Learning Visits' (no live document found in either export); mentoring duties (only when a Specialist is assigned as Mentor Specialist under Induction Module: Specialists 26-27 or as a Teacher Induction mentor — a conditional role, not every Specialist's weekly work); the Specialist induction year itself (applies to new Specialists only); Network Peer Review ('only when trained and assigned'); PD session delivery (Hook → Case → Input → Practice → Commitment, materials within 5 working days) because no live document dates the sessions; Programme Log updates (event-driven, covered by SS2-002); the November question-bank retire/flag check and the Department-meeting minutes, which are folded into SS2-009 and SS2-008.

Superseded source not used: 'Academic Board: Team Responsibilities - July 26' carries the footer 'Superseded — do not use as current guidance' (it still says A-EASE and DTP). Induction Module: Specialists 26-27 (Phase 5) says a certified Specialist becomes 'Primary Supervisor for two schools, Secondary Supervisor for two others, exactly as described in SS Guide Section 3's Eduversal School Support Model', but the Specialist Guide has no such model; the School Appraisal Overview uses Visit I / Visit II Supervisors with 3 schools each. I followed the School Appraisal documents; the induction text needs correcting.

Load (my simulation of the `when` rules over 36 teaching weeks): heaviest week is 3–7 May 2027 with 6 dated tasks (both monthly 'first' and 'last' tasks land there because May has one teaching week, plus Phase 4 and the annual review); 2–6 Nov 2026 has 5; most weeks have 1–4; 15–19 Feb and 12–16 Apr 2027 have none. Essentials: 5. Please re-run with the real seeder.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A short monthly subject brief from each Specialist to the Academic Director: top strengths, top risks, recommended actions.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The live documents give monthly school reviews and escalation of material risks, but no regular summary channel to the Academic Director between termly reviews; a short brief would also feed the CAO's Academic Quality Overview.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Annual Operating Calendar 26-27 (standing monthly rhythm)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A network-wide Cambridge results analysis per subject after each exam series (August for May/June, January for Oct/Nov).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Department Performance area D (Cambridge readiness) and the examiner-report routine exist, but no live document asks the Specialist to analyse the network's own Cambridge results by subject.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Specialist Guide 26-27 §7 (Reporting & Documentation Standards)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A one-page 'subject priorities for the year' note to all Subject Leaders at the start of the year (pacing expectations, key Cambridge changes, resource updates).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The July launch in the Operating Calendar sets up the Specialist's own system but nothing tells Subject Leaders the network priorities in writing; the first National Subject Department meeting could carry it.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Annual Operating Calendar 26-27 (July — Launch and baseline)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A regular (e.g. weekly) light presence in the subject's teacher community channel to answer questions and share resources.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Specialist Guide notes that silence in group chats is not evidence of competence; a named routine would make support visible between monthly meetings. The live weekly rhythm only says 'respond to questions'.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Minimum Operating Standard 26-27 §6 (Department and network operations)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Log visit logistics and travel within a set number of days after each visit.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Administrative only, but a clear deadline would keep travel records clean during the dense Phase 1 and Phase 3 windows.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Minimum Operating Standard 26-27 §9 (Minimum deadlines)
